question: A depressed patient has lost ten pounds, looks pale, and is fatigued. What is the best initial nursing action?

question: Which substance builds up in the joints to trigger a painful gout attack?

options.C: Excess synovial lubricating fluid

question: How do vaccines primarily protect the human body against infectious diseases?

question: What is the main sign of the bargaining stage?

question: What does sustainability mean for a community health program?

question: If a community shows both a high Maternal Mortality Ratio and a high Total Fertility Rate, what is the most likely link?

question: When we talk about improving quality of life in home care, what should be our main focus?

question: What is the main focus of holistic nursing care?

question: How can you, as a bedside nurse, help improve injection safety standards in your clinic?

question: What is the main job of the corpus luteum during the second half of the cycle?

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention?

explanation: Patient education saves lives! When patients know what red flags look like, they can get to the hospital fast before things get out of hand. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T32#GNS216_U5_T32_h7)

question: Which health issue is most commonly seen in patients taking second-generation antipsychotics long-term?

options.A: Metabolic syndrome and weight gain
options.B: Severe chronic renal failure
options.C: Chronic respiratory depression
options.D: Permanent hearing loss

explanation: Atypical antipsychotics are famous for changing metabolism. Patients often experience significant weight gain, changes in blood sugar, and altered cholesterol. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h4)

question: A public health nurse wants to know the total burden of chronic leukemia in a community, including people diagnosed years ago. Which measure should she look at?

options.A: Risk ratio
options.B: Prevalence
options.C: Incidence
options.D: Mortality rate

explanation: Prevalence measures all existing cases at a given time, capturing both new diagnoses and survivors living with the condition. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is depression in older adults frequently missed or left untreated?

options.A: Antidepressant medications work instantly in seniors
options.B: Symptoms are frequently mistaken for normal aging
options.C: Depression cures itself without any intervention
options.D: Older adults never experience depressive symptoms

explanation: It's sad but true—many people wrongly think that being withdrawn or feeling down is just 'part of growing old,' which causes them to miss treatable depression. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T5#GNS321_U3_T5_h8)

question: How do non-drug (non-pharmacological) methods help ease a patient's discomfort?

options.A: They permanently destroy local nerve endings
options.B: They chemically replace lost natural endorphins
options.C: They completely cure the underlying disease
options.D: They engage the mind and body to lower stress and pain signals

question: Which member of the theatre team is part of the sterile team?

options.A: Anaesthetist
options.B: Circulating nurse
options.C: Health orderly
options.D: Scrub nurse

explanation: The scrub nurse scrubs up, wears sterile gear, and handles sterile instruments right beside the surgeon. Think 'sterile zone, scrub nurse!' [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h1)

question: A student nurse is getting ready to irrigate an eye. Which action means they need a quick correction?

options.B: Encouraging the patient to blink periodically during the wash
options.C: Resting fingers directly upon the patient's eyeball to hold it open

question: When preparing a weaker cream from a stronger stock, what is your very first step?

options.A: Identify the starting strength and your target strength
options.B: Measure the patient's daily fluid intake and output
options.C: Throw away half of the total stock bottle immediately

question: Which of these actions is NOT allowed during a surgical hand scrub?

options.A: Using disposable picks to clean under your fingernails
options.B: Leaning against the sink edge to rest your arms
options.C: Keeping your hands higher than your elbows
options.D: Standing at a safe distance from the sink

question: A patient needs a nasogastric tube but has a history of a severe skull fracture at the base of the head. What should you do?

options.A: Perform the insertion quickly while the patient is asleep
options.B: Proceed with normal insertion using extra lubrication
options.C: Consult the doctor because putting a tube through the nose is risky here
options.D: Insert the tube through the mouth instead without checking

question: Which abnormal protein builds up inside the nerve cells in Pick's disease?

options.A: Tau protein
options.B: Beta-amyloid
options.C: Alpha-synuclein
options.D: Prion protein

explanation: Think of tau proteins as building blocks that go rogue and clump up inside the brain cells in Pick's disease. Knowing this pathology makes the rest of the topic much easier to master! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T6#GNS222_U4_T6_h2)

question: Why must a nurse use a separate measuring cylinder for each patient when emptying drainage bags?

options.A: To stop the plastic containers from wearing out too quickly
options.B: To prevent cross-contamination and spread of infections between patients
options.C: To make measuring the fluid much faster during busy shifts
options.D: To ensure the hospital records look neat and well-organized

explanation: Infection control 101! Using dedicated equipment for every patient keeps germs from hitching a ride across the ward. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h5)

question: A patient tells you she feels a heavy dragging sensation in her pelvis after having three children. What structures are likely stretched or weakened?

options.A: The Bartholin glands located near the vaginal opening
options.B: Ligaments and pelvic floor muscles supporting the uterus
options.C: The fimbriae at the ends of the fallopian tubes
options.D: The fallopian tubes where fertilization usually occurs

explanation: You're doing great! When pelvic floor muscles and support ligaments get stretched over time, they can lead to uterine prolapse, causing that heavy, dragging feeling. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h8)

question: What is the most common cause of blunt upper airway trauma in adults?

options.A: Sudden throat infections
options.B: Spontaneous tissue tears
options.C: Motor vehicle collisions
options.D: Severe allergic reactions

explanation: Spot on! Direct impacts from steering wheels or dashboards during car crashes frequently compress neck structures against the spine. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T5#GNS213_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why do healthcare facilities conduct regular fire and disaster drills?

options.A: To frighten new students so they stay alert on the ward
options.B: To ensure staff can respond calmly and efficiently during an actual crisis
options.C: To give the maintenance team a chance to test the lights
options.D: To fulfill insurance rules without teaching staff any real skills

explanation: Regular practice builds muscle memory and confidence so healthcare workers follow evacuation and safety steps automatically during a real emergency. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h7)

question: What protective layer of cells surrounds a secondary oocyte when it is released during ovulation?

options.A: Myometrium lining
options.B: Endometrial stroma
options.C: Amniotic membrane
options.D: Corona radiata

explanation: The corona radiata is a supportive halo of follicular cells wrapped around the egg that incoming sperm must work through during fertilization. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h2)

question: Why are broad-spectrum antibiotics started immediately before lab test results come back?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any follow-up blood tests
options.B: To prevent the patient from experiencing allergic reactions
options.C: To prevent rapid progression and permanent tubal damage
options.D: To destroy normal vaginal flora permanently

explanation: Acting fast stops the infection in its tracks, helping to protect the tubes from long-term damage. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h6)

question: What is the simplest way to describe what a drug does in the body?

options.A: Any synthetic material used strictly for laboratory testing
options.B: A compound that creates entirely new cellular functions in organs
options.C: Any chemical substance that alters biological function in a living body
options.D: A natural substance derived exclusively from plants for nourishment

question: Where do the bones of your skull and jaw mostly come from during early development?

options.A: Visceral endoderm
options.B: Neural crest cells
options.C: Pelvic mesoderm
options.D: Cardiac jelly

explanation: Think of neural crest cells as great travelers—they migrate forward into the head region early on to form your face and skull bones! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T1#GNS121_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why should you stay right by the patient's side until they swallow their oral pills?

options.A: To clean up the empty plastic medication cup immediately
options.B: To engage in friendly conversation and build a strong therapeutic bond
options.C: To ensure the patient actually takes the drug rather than hiding or discarding it
options.D: To make sure the patient drinks an entire pitcher of cold water

explanation: Leaving pills at the bedside can lead to missed doses or accidental ingestion by visiting children. Always watch them swallow! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T1#GNS125_U4_T1_h6)

question: How can a nurse best support self-advocacy in a patient with a physical disability?

options.A: By making all medical and lifestyle decisions on behalf of the patient
options.B: By encouraging the patient to voice their own healthcare choices and rights
options.C: By shielding the patient from interacting with unfamiliar community members
options.D: By filing formal legal complaints without consulting the patient first

explanation: Self-advocacy grows when nurses empower patients to speak up and make their own informed decisions about care and life. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h8)

question: What is the best way to count a patient's respiratory rate accurately without making them change how they breathe?

options.A: Announce loudly that you are starting to count breaths now
options.B: Count respirations discreetly right after taking the radial pulse without moving your hand away
options.C: Place a heavy hand on their chest to feel every rib movement
options.D: Ask them to take ten deep breaths so you can time it

explanation: Smart nursing! Patients often change their breathing if they know you're watching. Transitioning straight from the pulse keeps their breathing natural. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T4#GNS123_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of performing a neurological examination?

options.A: To determine the exact blood type of the patient
options.B: To measure the patient's daily caloric intake
options.C: To diagnose specific psychiatric disorders
options.D: To evaluate the function of the nervous system

explanation: The neurological exam is specifically designed to assess how well the central and peripheral nervous systems are working. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the main reason for doing passive range of motion exercises on a bedbound patient?

options.A: To directly build large muscle mass in the limbs
options.B: To prevent joint contractures and maintain flexibility
options.C: To cure underlying systemic cardiovascular disease
options.D: To eliminate the need for any future physical therapy

explanation: You've got this! Moving joints gently keeps them from getting stiff and locked up when patients can't move themselves. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T5#GNS123_U6_T5_h4)

question: How has our view of leadership in healthcare changed over time?

options.A: From team collaboration to absolute individual control by doctors
options.B: From flexible behaviors to rigid, unchanging personal traits
options.C: From clinical skills to purely financial management tasks
options.D: From fixed personal traits to flexible behaviors and situational responses

explanation: We used to think leaders were just born with special traits. Now, we know good leaders adapt their style to fit whatever is happening on the ward! [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h1)

question: While checking a patient with a leg infection, you notice their toes are cool, pale, and slow to refill with blood. What is your best first move?

options.B: Document the findings as normal post-surgical swelling
options.C: Encourage the patient to get out of bed and walk
options.D: Report the neurovascular changes to the physician immediately

question: What is the approximate time it takes to complete a standard barium swallow procedure?

options.A: Exactly 5 minutes
options.B: 2 to 3 hours

explanation: Most standard barium swallow exams are relatively quick, taking between a quarter to half an hour depending on patient cooperation and findings. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of occupational health surveillance?

options.A: To punish workers who report feeling sick on the job
options.B: To catch early signs of work-related illness through regular testing
options.C: To calculate the exact salary of every factory worker
options.D: To replace the need for engineering safety barriers

explanation: Surveillance monitors worker health over time so that illnesses can be detected and treated early before causing permanent damage. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h7)

question: Why is careful monitoring of IV fluids especially vital during labor for a mother with kidney disease?

options.A: Excess fluids stop the uterus from contracting normally after the baby is born
options.B: Compromised kidneys cannot handle fluid overload, increasing the risk of pulmonary edema
options.C: Too much intravenous fluid causes the infant's kidneys to stop working permanently
options.D: Intravenous fluids react badly with standard pain medications used in labor

question: What piece of info is automatically attached to every single entry you make in an EMR?

options.C: The user login ID, date, and exact timestamp

question: A nurse is discharging a patient who had a bowel obstruction from Crohn's disease. Which symptom should the nurse flag as an urgent emergency?

options.A: Feeling tired during normal daily physical activities
options.B: Mild gas and bloating after eating a small meal
options.C: Severe, unrelenting abdominal pain and persistent vomiting
options.D: A slight increase in daily bowel movement frequency

question: A patient recovering from surgery suddenly complains of severe shortness of breath and sharp chest pain. What emergency should the nurse suspect first?

question: Which blood test is usually checked first when doctors suspect a thyroid problem?

options.A: Total serum calcium

question: A patient recovering from a stroke can clearly see a pen on the table and describe its color and shape, but cannot name it or tell you what it's for. Which part of their brain is likely affected?

question: What is a main goal of visiting a mother at home during the postnatal period?

question: Why must a pregnant woman report blurred vision and a terrible headache immediately?

options.C: They show that the baby is moving too much inside
options.D: They indicate severe high blood pressure or pre-eclampsia

question: What is a key piece of advice specifically for clients taking progestin-only mini-pills?

question: Why are old writings from figures like Hippocrates and Pliny so important to occupational health?

options.C: They forced emperors to pass the first fair labor acts

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of acute salpingitis?

question: What is the main goal behind food processing and preservation?

question: What causes the microfilariae to leave the skin sample and enter the liquid?

question: How do rushed staff and chaotic hospital environments affect patients?

question: What is the most common cause of a physical small bowel blockage in adults who have had previous tummy surgery?

question: Why are older adults much more prone to chronic dehydration?

question: What is the main focus during the evaluation phase of the nursing process?

options.A: Gathering baseline lab results before surgery

question: What is the main goal of antenatal care (ANC) services for a pregnant mother?

options.C: Monitor normal pregnancy and detect early complications
options.D: Guarantee a completely pain-free labor experience

question: When should you ideally start planning for a neurological client's discharge?

question: What would an occupational therapist most likely help a recovering stroke patient do?

options.C: Navigating financial assistance for home medical equipment

question: Why is the operating suite usually tucked away from busy hospital hallways?

question: What is the main purpose of the clay and plastic lining inside a sanitary landfill?

options.C: To attract earthworms that break down plastic materials
options.D: To prevent toxic liquid leachate from reaching underground water

question: You just received a new delivery of canned milk for the clinic pantry. Where should you put the new cans?

question: What is the golden rule for feeding an infant during their first six months of life?

question: How should a nurse present different contraceptive choices to a client?

question: What is the primary purpose of bereavement support after a patient passes away?

question: Which of these is NOT a red flag symptom that requires medical investigation? (Find the exception)

question: When caring for a patient at home who isn't eating well, what is a common mistake people make?

question: Which of these is a classic sign that a patient might have hypothyroidism?

options.C: Excessive nervousness and tremors

question: What is the primary purpose of performing a straight leg raise test on a patient complaining of back pain?

options.C: To measure the exact range of motion of the hip joint

question: What is the primary advantage of intravenous therapy over oral medication administration?

question: Which part of the nervous system takes over during non-REM sleep to slow your heart rate and lower blood pressure?

question: You suspect a patient is skipping their blood pressure meds because their readings are still high. How should you start this chat?

options.A: I know you forgot your pills because your blood pressure is still high.
options.B: If you do not start taking your medicine today, you will suffer a stroke.
options.C: Why are you wasting your money by refusing to take your prescribed drugs?
options.D: Many people find it hard to take pills every day; tell me about your routine.

explanation: Brilliant choice! Normalizing the struggle takes away shame and helps the patient open up honestly to you. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which physical assessment technique is used to check for kidney tenderness at the back?

options.A: Inspection
options.B: Percussion
options.C: Retraction
options.D: Auscultation

explanation: Great job! Gently tapping (percussing) the costovertebral angle at the back helps us check if the kidneys are inflamed or tender. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why do healthcare workers perform an Allen test before drawing an arterial blood gas (ABG) sample?

options.A: To verify adequate collateral circulation to the hand
options.B: To numb the puncture site before inserting the needle
options.C: To measure the exact blood pressure in the radial artery
options.D: To check if the patient has a bleeding disorder

explanation: The Allen test makes sure the hand has a backup blood supply (from the ulnar artery) just in case the radial artery gets blocked during the needle puncture. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T7#GNS123_U2_T7_h7)

question: What drives the extremely fast skin cell growth seen in plaque psoriasis?

options.A: Cold weather triggers massive mast cell breakdown
options.B: The body attacks and destroys pigment cells in the base layer
options.C: Bacteria directly eat away at the outer skin layer
options.D: T-cells release chemical signals that speed up skin cell division

explanation: In psoriasis, hyperactive T-cells release inflammatory chemicals that tell skin cells to multiply way too fast, piling up into those thick, silvery scales. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h6)

question: What do we call bundles of nerve fibers found entirely inside the central nervous system?

options.A: Ganglia
options.B: Tracts
options.C: Nerves
options.D: Receptors

explanation: Great to know for exams: inside the brain and spinal cord, fiber bundles are called tracts. Outside the central nervous system, we call them nerves! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T16#GNS211_U3_T16_h2)

question: What is the main muscle cell that makes up the heart wall?

options.A: Osteocyte
options.B: Nephron
options.C: Cardiocyte
options.D: Neuron

explanation: You've got this! A cardiocyte is simply the individual muscle cell found in cardiac tissue. Nephrons are in the kidneys, neurons in the brain, and osteocytes in bones. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T10#GNS121_U3_T10_h1)

question: Which type of uterine fibroid is most likely to cause trouble with a fertilized egg trying to implant?

options.A: Intramural fibroids
options.B: Subserosal fibroids
options.C: Pedunculated fibroids
options.D: Submucosal fibroids

explanation: Brilliant! Submucosal fibroids grow right inside the main cavity of the womb, messing directly with the inner lining where pregnancy needs to begin. You've got this! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h4)

question: How does artificial intelligence help out in advanced EMR systems?

options.A: Setting the room temperature based on patient preference
options.B: Automatically writing hospital discharge summaries without human review
options.C: Replacing the head nurse with a computerized management algorithm
options.D: Analyzing vital sign trends to help predict complications like sepsis early

explanation: Smart algorithms scan patient data behind the scenes to warn the care team of subtle signs of danger before things get critical. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h7)

question: Which of these actions is WRONG when responding to a cardiac arrest in a patient with skull traction?

options.A: Keeping the neck in neutral alignment during all emergency maneuvers
options.B: Ensuring a doctor or emergency team member manages the head position
options.C: Removing the traction weights immediately to start chest compressions
options.D: Following hospital guidelines for emergency airway management

explanation: Never just yank the weights off in a panic! Removing them suddenly can cause the injured neck to snap out of place. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h7)

question: What is the main goal of a Rapid Response Team in the hospital?

options.A: To intervene early when a patient shows signs of rapid decline
options.B: To perform routine morning vital sign checks
options.C: To replace physicians during surgical procedures
options.D: To audit patient charts for billing compliance

explanation: Spot on! Rapid response teams bring critical care expertise straight to the bedside the moment a patient starts slipping, helping prevent full cardiac arrest. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T11#GNS123_U5_T11_h6)

question: What is the main goal of a community's 'production, distribution, and consumption' function?

options.A: Providing free hospital care to every citizen
options.B: Teaching cultural values to children in school buildings
options.C: Enforcing criminal laws and maintaining local police stations
options.D: Meeting the basic survival and economic needs of members

explanation: You've got it! This is simply about making sure people have access to food, shelter, and the basics needed to survive every day. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T4#GNS225_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of critical care nursing?

options.A: Long-term management of stable chronic illnesses at home
options.B: Outpatient screening for common infectious diseases
options.C: Care of patients with unstable, life-threatening conditions
options.D: Routine post-surgical rehabilitation and physical therapy

explanation: Critical care nursing is specifically dedicated to patients whose conditions are unstable and require intensive monitoring. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h1)

question: How do accurate nursing medication records help support the DRF scheme?

options.A: They allow the hospital to charge patients double for every injection
options.B: They help pharmacists accurately forecast future drug consumption needs
options.C: They replace the need for physical stock counts in the pharmacy
options.D: They prove to the nursing council that staff are writing clearly

explanation: Wonderful! Clear records from the wards show exactly what patients are using, helping the pharmacy order the right amounts without guesswork. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T8#GNS223_U3_T8_h7)

question: Why must a nurse tape all tubing connections securely right after a chest tube is put in?

options.A: To increase the speed of fluid drainage into the collection chamber
options.B: To stop the patient from bending the tubing during sleep
options.C: To prevent the water in the seal chamber from evaporating away
options.D: To prevent accidental disconnection and a collapsed lung

explanation: Loose connections can let room air slip into the chest, which can quickly turn into a dangerous emergency. Always double-check your joints! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T15#GNS213_U2_T15_h4)
